description: Ali Safari Khatouni and colleagues publish mobile-broadband speedtest traces collected mainly in Turin, Italy. The June 2017 Zenodo deposit covers WiFi, 3G and 4G connections from participating smartphone users travelling by public or private vehicles. Experiments use iperf2 uploads with TCP or UDP and passive server-side packet capture through tcpdump, normally for 600 seconds. The ZIP archive is freely available under CC BY 4.0. These traces can calibrate mobile-throughput models or test network-performance simulations under movement. Some shorter traces represent stationary MONROE tests or failed experiments, so they should not be pooled indiscriminately with mobile runs. Exact collection dates, sample counts and device balance remain unknown from the public summary. No related catalogue record explicitly covers the collection. Traces were not downloaded, and the historical technologies do not represent current 5G performance.
